wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive getting started content for ContentOS, a full-stack content management system built with Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, and Prisma. Address common setup issues and provide troubleshooting guidance for first-time users.

# ContentOS: A Comprehensive Content Management Platform

## Project Introduction

ContentOS is a modern content management platform built with Next.js that serves as a complete "content operating system" for creators and marketers. The application provides an integrated workspace for planning, creating, scheduling, and publishing content across multiple platforms with AI-powered assistance.

### Core Goals and Objectives
- **Unified Content Workflow**: Streamline the entire content creation process from ideation to publication
- **Multi-Platform Publishing**: Support for various social media platforms through a centralized interface
- **AI-Powered Creation**: Leverage artificial intelligence to assist in content generation and optimization
- **Scheduling & Automation**: Enable automated content publishing at optimal times
- **Analytics Integration**: Provide insights into content performance across platforms

### Target Audience
- Content creators and marketers
- Social media managers
- Digital marketing teams
- Content strategists seeking automation tools

## Technical Architecture

The application follows a modern Next.js 16 architecture with server-side rendering capabilities and a comprehensive database schema managed through Prisma ORM.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Next.js App Router] --> B[Server Components]
    A --> C[API Routes]
    B --> D[Workspace Layout]
    C --> E[Database Layer]
    E --> F[(PostgreSQL)]
    
    G[Client Components] --> H[UI State Management]
    I[Media Upload] --> J[File System Storage]
    K[Publishing Engine] --> L[External APIs]
    
    D --> M[Content Management]
    D --> N[Calendar Scheduling]
    D --> O[AI Studio]
    D --> P[Analytics Dashboard]
```

### Component Breakdown

The application is structured around several key architectural patterns:

**Server-Side Rendering (SSR)**: Utilizes Next.js server components for data fetching and initial page rendering
**Component Composition**: Reusable UI components organized by feature areas
**API Route Handlers**: RESTful endpoints for client-server communication
**Database Abstraction**: Prisma ORM providing type-safe database operations
**State Management**: Client-side state using React hooks and context

### Design Patterns

- **Repository Pattern**: Database operations encapsulated in Prisma models
- **Component-Based Architecture**: Modular UI components with clear separation of concerns
- **Event-Driven Publishing**: Asynchronous content publishing workflow
- **Middleware Pattern**: Request processing and validation in API routes

## Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points

**Application Root** (`app/layout.tsx`): Configures global fonts, metadata, and application shell structure with Geist and Inter font families for consistent typography.

**Home Page** (`app/page.tsx`): Server component that fetches dashboard statistics including idea counts, content metrics, published items, and connected channels, passing data to the client component.

**Content Management** (`app/content/page.tsx`): Implements the main content library view with filtering, sorting, and navigation capabilities, showcasing the workspace layout pattern used throughout the application.

### Core Modules

**Database Schema** (`prisma/schema.prisma`): Defines the complete data model including Idea, Content, Media, PublishingChannel, and Publication entities with proper relationships and constraints.

**Media Upload Handler** (`app/api/media/upload/route.ts`): Handles file uploads with validation, size limits (50MB), type restrictions, and storage management, demonstrating secure file handling practices.

**Publishing Engine** (`app/publishing/engine/process-scheduled.ts`): Implements scheduled content publishing with batch processing, error handling, and status tracking for queued publications.

### Configuration Approach

**Package Management** (`package.json`): Modern dependency management with Next.js 16, React 19, Prisma 7, and PostgreSQL adapter, along with development tools like Tailwind CSS v4 and TypeScript.

**Database Configuration** (`lib/prisma.ts`): Centralized Prisma client initialization with PostgreSQL connection management.

### External Dependencies

Key dependencies include:
- **Next.js 16**: React framework with App Router and server components
- **React 19**: Latest React version with concurrent features
- **Prisma 7**: Type-safe database toolkit with PostgreSQL support
- **Tailwind CSS v4**: Utility-first CSS framework for styling
- **GSAP**: Animation library for smooth user interactions
- **PostgreSQL**: Primary database for persistent storage

### Integration Points

**AI Integration**: Structured API routes for AI-powered content generation (`app/api/ai/`)
**Social Media Platforms**: Publishing channel abstraction supporting LinkedIn and simulated platforms
**File Storage**: Local file system integration for media assets with proper cleanup and organization

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    Client->>+API Route: Upload Media
    API Route->>+Validation: Validate File
    Validation-->>-API Route: Valid/Invalid
    API Route->>+Storage: Save File
    Storage-->>-API Route: File Path
    API Route->>+Database: Create Media Record
    Database-->>-API Route: Success
    API Route-->>-Client: Upload Response
```

## Key Features

### Functionality Overview

**Content Lifecycle Management**: Complete workflow from idea capture through content creation, editing, scheduling, and publication with status tracking and version control.

**Multi-Platform Publishing**: Abstracted publishing engine supporting multiple social media platforms with unified interface and platform-specific optimizations.

**AI-Powered Content Creation**: Integrated AI studio for generating content ideas, writing assistance, and content optimization suggestions.

**Visual Calendar Interface**: Drag-and-drop scheduling interface for planning content publication timelines with conflict detection and resource allocation.

### Implementation Highlights

**Workspace Layout System** (`components/layout/workspace-layout.tsx`): Responsive layout with collapsible sidebar, top navigation bar, and adaptive content areas that maintain context across different sections.

**Real-time Analytics**: Dashboard components providing insights into content performance, engagement metrics, and publishing effectiveness with customizable reporting.

**Media Management**: Comprehensive media library with upload, preview, and organization capabilities supporting images, videos, and various file formats.

### Feature Architecture

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idea
    Idea --> Draft: Convert to Content
    Draft --> Editing: Edit Content
    Editing --> Scheduled: Schedule Publication
    Scheduled --> Published: Auto Publish
    Scheduled --> Rescheduled: Modify Schedule
    Published --> Archived: Post-Publication
    
    Note right of Idea: Capture & Organize Ideas
    Note right of Draft: Initial Content Creation
    Note right of Editing: Refine & Optimize
    Note right of Scheduled: Queue for Publishing
    Note right of Published: Live on Platforms
```

The application demonstrates modern web development best practices with a focus on scalability, maintainability, and user experience. The modular architecture allows for easy extension of functionality while maintaining code organization and performance optimization.
